priority_papers_requested: McCann 2020 - Is there anything toxic about femininity

mccann_2020_toxic_femininity.title: Is there anything 'toxic' about femininity? The rigid femininities that keep us locked in
mccann_2020_toxic_femininity.source: Taylor & Francis / Minerva Access University of Melbourne
mccann_2020_toxic_femininity.abstract: This paper interrogates the concept of 'toxic femininity', examining how rigid femininity norms constrain women. Argues that rather than femininity being inherently toxic, it is the rigid enforcement of feminine norms that creates harm. Uses feminist theory to unpack how femininity operates as a regulatory mechanism.
mccann_2020_toxic_femininity.key_argument: Critiques the concept of 'toxic femininity' arguing that femininity itself is not toxic but the rigid enforcement of feminine norms creates harm. Femininity operates as a regulatory mechanism limiting women's agency and choices.

problematising_toxic_masculinity_2019.key_argument: Critically examines the toxic/healthy masculinity binary, problematizing how these categories are constructed and used in gender equality work.

api_notes: Semantic Scholar API frequently returned empty results for many queries - possible rate limiting or query issues
OpenAlex API proved more reliable, returned results for gender ideology queries
arXiv returned limited feminist NLP papers, mostly HCI/feminist AI ethics papers
Google Scholar scrape blocked at headers stage
research_gaps_identified: Limited academic papers specifically addressing 'toxic femininity' as a standalone construct (most papers are 2018-2025)
System justification theory applied specifically to anti-feminist backlash is underdeveloped (Yeung 2013 not found specifically)
Misandry detection NLP is a significant research gap with no clear papers found
Feminist infighting/faction papers are rare in mainstream databases - more likely in grey literature
